Homage to Śrī Gaṇeśa.
Oṃ, homage to the goddess Śrī Siddhilakṣmī.
Oṃ hrīṃ hraṃ hāṃ preṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ.
Oṃ hrīṃ hraḥ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ namaḥ.
Oṃ hrīṃ hraṃ hāṃ phreṃ oṃ kroṃ namaḥ.
Oṃ tatsat || Oṃ tatsat || Oṃ tatsat ||

Oṃ. Of this mantra of the Garland of Letters (Yutākṣaramālā) associated with the Illustrious Siddhilakṣmī, Bharadvāja is the seer (ṛṣi); the meters (chandas) are Madhyā, Pratiṣṭhā, Supratiṣṭhā, Gāyatrī, Uṣṇik, Anuṣṭubh, Bṛhatī, Paṅkti, Triṣṭubh, Jagatī, Paṅkti, Jagatī, Śarkarī, Atiśarkarī, Prakṛti, and Ut-kṛti.
Siddhi is the goddess Lakṣmī; *phreṃ* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*).
Khphreṃ is the Śakti; Kroṃ is the Kīlaka; this is for the purpose of attaining the siddhis of enjoyment and liberation during the application of recitation (japa).

2a) Aiṃ Oṃ Hrīṃ Hraṃ Phreṃ! O Blessed Caṇḍakāpālinī, Siddhilakṣmī, Pratyāṅgirā! Kṣoṃ Kroṃ Śrīṃ Strīṃ! O You of the red face, You who laugh with a terrible roar, You who utter a fearsome sound, You who remove the suffering of those who bow before You!
Āṃ krīṃ hoṃ kṣoṃ gloṃ! O dweller in the cremation ground, whose body is as radiant as the moon!
O you who ferry across the multitude of devotees! Phreṃ Khphreṃ Hsphreṃ Hskhphreṃ Hsauṃ!
O you who move in the state of essential identity with the supreme Sadāśiva! O Kātyāyanī! O Kāpālinī! O Great Yoginī!
O you who are whiter than jasmine and the moon! O you who are mounted upon the corpse of Mahābhadra’s form!
Krauṃ Oṃ Gluṃ Glauṃ Vlūṃ, O you who delight the minds of all gods, asuras, humans, and kinnaras!
2b) O crusher of the pride of the Daityas and Dānavas!
O bearer of five faces!
O you who wear a garland of human skulls! O you who are captivating!
Bestowing the fruits of the fourfold aims of human life.
To her who sings with rhythmic clapping of hands and dancing.
Hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ hraṃ hrauṃ! O you of most fierce and exceedingly terrible, great, and horrific roar!
She who illuminates the knowledge of the threefold great reality.
O you who cause terror to the fourteen worlds, O Great Laughter!
Trīṃ thrīṃ drīṃ dhrīṃ nrīṃ! Adorned with ten staff-like arms that are bold in granting fearlessness to the three worlds!
In the beautiful left eye of Bhūteśvara, which brings about supreme sovereignty, three eyes shine resplendently.
Phe & Phre & Khphre & Hsphre & Hskhphre & Himakundadhavalakalevare 'pi Mahānīlanīradaprabhe Pratyaṅgirā Śaktitattvāvatāre!
3a) In that which is extremely fierce, terrifying, and most fearsome;
In the three worlds terrified by the convention of the rhythmic clapping of hands that dangle and swing.
O cause of the accumulation of sins gathered through many births, within the waters of the great ocean of hell!
Hrīṃ Hūṃ Phreṃ Oṃ Kroṃ! O Royal Fortune, O Victory Fortune! Conquer, conquer! Live, live! Speak, speak!
O Great Illusion, who shatters all enemies with a flash of light!
Hrīṃ hūṃ phreṃ phaṭ! O you who swallow ten million cosmic eggs with a great roar!
3b) Hrīṃ Hūṃ Phreṃ Phaṭ! O you who consist of the state of supreme identity with Śiva, O Great Terrifying One!
Hrīṃ hūṃ phreṃ phaṭ! O you who wander through the great cremation grounds, O highly fortunate one!
Hrīṃ Hūṃ Phreṃ Phaṭ! O you who shatter the suffering of great poverty, O Great Laughter!
Hrīṃ hūṃ phreṃ phaṭ! O you who are the form of absolute liberation, O illuminator of your own state, O Great Terrible One!
Hrīṃ hūṃ phreṃ phaṭ! O Mahācaṇḍā, bestower of the fruits of the four aims of human life!
Hrīṃ hūṃ phreṃ phaṭ! O you who are radiant with the weight of a great mass of matted hair, O Great Devourer!
Hrīṃ hūṃ phreṃ phaṭ! O Mistress of the entire wheel of Kula and Akula, O Great Compassionate One!
4a) Hrīṃ hūṃ phreṃ phaṭ! O Mahāvidyā, whose body consists of the qualities of pure sattva!
Hrīṃ hūṃ phreṃ phaṭ! O liberator from the bonds of saṃsāra, you who transcend all parts!
Hrīṃ hūṃ phreṃ phaṭ! In the great light, which is the abode fashioned by the five fires of time.
Hrīṃ Hūṃ Phreṃ Phaṭ! O you who are adorned with the circle of great staff-like arms, in the abode of Rudra!
Hrīṃ Hūṃ Phreṃ Phaṭ! O you who bestow protection upon the fourteen worlds, O you of great power!
Hrīṃ hūṃ phreṃ phaṭ! O you of terrible form with a blazing fire-face, O you of the great vow!
Hrīṃ hūṃ phreṃ phaṭ! O crusher of the sons of Diti and Danu, in the great aeon!
Hrīṃ hūṃ phreṃ phaṭ! O Great Dancer, whose power was manifested in the Satya Yuga!
4b) Hrīṃ hūṃ phreṃ phaṭ! O you who rest in the auspicious cross-legged posture, who are victorious in battle, and who are absorbed in the supreme Brahman!
Oṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ, homage to her who moves in the company of the Supreme Śiva, who wears a garland of human skulls,
and who brings about the fulfillment of all desires!
Oṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ, homage to the one whose body is as white as a conch shell, camphor, cow’s milk, and snow— pure, bright, long, and sharp—
who is the crooked lord of the gods, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and the other deities, the one who dwells in the state beyond the senses.
Oṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ, homage to her who bestows all auspiciousness, who confers various and complete sovereign powers,
and who reclines upon the body of her own beloved in the form of a corpse.
Oṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ, homage to you whose body consists of nine crores of mantras, who have accomplished the subjugation of all the daityas, and who have extended grace to your devotees.
Oṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ, homage to you whose eyes are the moon, sun, and fire; who liberates one from the bonds of saṃsāra; and who illuminates all the scriptures.

Oṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ, homage to her who dwells in the most terrifying wilderness, who produces fear in the three worlds with her dreadful laughter, and who revels in the state of aesthetic union with Supreme Śiva.
Oṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ, homage to you whose power is renowned in the Vedas and Vedāntas;
you who cause terror to those seated upon the great cremation ground, and who possess a most formidable roar.
Oṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ, homage! O you who have uprooted all adverse factors through the conceptualization of emanation, abiding, and withdrawal; O protector of devoted followers who are thus established!

Oṃ kṣo& kro& namaḥ! O you who are neither too tall nor short, yet full-figured; O you who wear the net of the time of universal dissolution as your garment; O you who are clothed in the garments of the great cremation ground!

Oṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ, homage! She who is clothed in a tiger-skin garment, whose hips are girt, who is like the great dissolution at the end of time, and who is the martial heroine of the single expanse of the seven oceans.
Oṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ, homage! Victory, victory, O Great Mistress of Yoga, born of yoga, attainable through yoga, transcending yoga, whose form is yoga!
6a) Śrīṃ Klīṃ Strīṃ Svāhā! Victory, victory, O Sovereign of Great Knowledge, born of knowledge, attainable through knowledge, beyond the known, whose very form is knowledge!
Śrīṃ Klīṃ Strīṃ Svāhā! Victory, victory, O Great Mistress of Mantras, born of mantra, attainable through mantra, transcending mantra, whose very form is mantra!
Śrīṃ Klīṃ Strīṃ Svāhā! Victory, victory, O Great Sovereign of All! O Source of All! O One accessible by all! O One transcending all! O You who are the form of all!
Śrīṃ Klīṃ Strīṃ Svāhā! Victory, victory, O Sovereign of Dharma, born of Dharma, accessible through Dharma, transcending Dharma, whose very form is Dharma!
6b) Śrīṃ Klīṃ Strīṃ Svāhā! Victory, victory, O Great Mistress of Desire, born of desire, accessible through desire, transcending desire, whose form is desire!
Śrīṃ Klīṃ Strīṃ Svāhā! Victory, victory, O Sovereign of Great Liberation! O Source of liberation, O Goal of liberation, O That which transcends liberation, O Embodiment of liberation!
Śrīṃ Klīṃ Strīṃ Svāhā! Victory, victory, O Sovereign of Great Nirvāṇa! O You who are born from Nirvāṇa, who are the goal of Nirvāṇa, who transcend Nirvāṇa, and whose very form is Nirvāṇa!
Śrīṃ Klīṃ Strīṃ Svāhā! Victory, victory, O Great Kaivalyeśvarī! O You who are born of Kaivalya, who are to be attained through Kaivalya, who transcend Kaivalya, and whose very form is Kaivalya!
chrīṃ klīṃ strīṃ svāhā ||
Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ jaya jaya jīva jīva triśūlini mahābalini hūṃ phaṭ namaḥ svāhā.

Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ, victory, victory! Live, live! O you who delude the supreme Sadāśiva who transcends all qualities; O you who delight in the essence of liberation; O you who grow from the consciousness-bliss of the quality of pure sattva! Hūṃ phaṭ! Namaḥ svāhā! Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ, victory, victory! Live, live! O Great King of Nagas!
Hūṃ Phaṭ Namaḥ Svāhā! O you who adorn your ten mighty arms; O you who have severed the bodies of all the Daityas and Dānavas with your fiercely blazing sword;
O you who incessantly draw your formidable bow and arrows! Hūṃ Phaṭ Namaḥ Svāhā!
Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ! Victory, victory! Live, live! O you who are beyond the reach of mind, senses, and speech;
O you whose every limb consists of the three qualities; O you whose garment is a tiger skin! Hūṃ phaṭ! Homage! Svāhā!
Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ! Victory, victory! Live, live! O you who are radiant with the burden of your most trembling matted locks;
you who possess a throat as soft as snow, jasmine, the moon, and camphor; you who shatter the noose of the saṃsāra of old age, birth, and death! Hūṃ phaṭ! Homage! Svāhā!

Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ! Victory, victory! Live, live! O you who have ascended to the reality of the Śiva-Śakti principle, which is both supreme and non-supreme, and is more secret than the most secret; O you who abide in the state of self-bliss and the station of self-luminosity;
O you who are seated upon the couch of the play of aesthetic equilibrium (sāmarasya)! Hūṃ phaṭ! Homage! Svāhā!

7b) Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ, victory, victory! Live, live! O you who transcend both primordial nature and the individual soul, witness of the supreme good, protector of the three worlds, devourer of daityas and dānavas! Hūṃ phaṭ! Homage! Svāhā!
Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ! Victory, victory! Live, live! O you who set in motion the wheel of the entire Kaula doctrine;
O Great Plague who causes terror to all Daityas, Dānavas, and Rākṣasas; O you who avert the fear of foreign armies, famine, and great portents! Hūṃ phaṭ! Homage! Svāhā!

Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ! Victory, victory! Live, live! O you who have reached the further shore of the application of various divine weapons; O bird within the cage consisting of mantras of the six traditions;
O you who have made all bodies your ornaments; O you who possess eight serpents as your adornments; hūṃ phaṭ! Homage! Svāhā!

Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ! Victory, victory! Live, live! O you who transcend all phenomenal expansion, O you whose form is the partless fourth state (turīya), O stream of nectar consisting of the awakening of the Supreme Self which is unbroken bliss, O essence of the truth of the Vedas and Agamas! Hūṃ phaṭ!
Homage! Svāhā!

Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ, victory, victory! O Jīva, Jīva! O Mahākhecarī, bestower of the eight supernatural powers (*pratisiddhi*); O Goddess, nectar arisen from the ocean of milk, drinker of the special essence;
O Illusion (*māyinī*), who causes the binding of the vital breaths produced within the belly of the three worlds; hūṃ phaṭ, obeisance, svāhā!

Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hāṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ! Victory, victory! Live, live! O you whose lotus feet are worthy of worship by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva; O you whose neck is adorned with a garland of human heads; O you who are unbearable to all gods and asuras and possess great power! Hūṃ phaṭ! Homage! Svāhā!
Victory, victory to you, O Pratyaṅgirā, in the Age of Truth!
Victory, victory, O Siddhilakṣmī of the Tretā Yuga!
Victory, victory, O Royal Fortune in the Dvāpara Age!
Victory, victory to you, O fierce Kāpālinī of the Kali age!

Oṃ aiṃ āṃ hsauṃ sauṃ! O Blessed One, be gracious, be gracious! Blaze, blaze! Flare up, flare up! Quiver, quiver! Tremble, tremble! Crack, crack! Crackle, crackle! Sing, sing! Laugh, laugh! Dance, dance! Roar, roar! Kili kili! Kici kici! Hasten, hasten! Run, run! Hūṃ phreṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ hrīṃ Vyomake!
O you who are endowed with splendor, O you with tawny hair, phaṭ svāhā!
10a) HŪM PHREṂ KṢOṂ KROṂ HRĪṂ BHAGAMĀLINI BHAGAPRADE BHAGAPRIYE PHAṬ SVĀHĀ ||
HŪM PHREṂ KṢOṂ KROṂ HRĪṂ! O you who are intoxicated with passion, who devour the flesh of corpses, who converse with Brahmā! PHAṬ SVĀHĀ!
HŪM PHREṂ KṢOṂ KROṂ HRĪṂ! O you who are adorned with a garland of human skulls, who ferry beings across the ocean of saṃsāra, whose feet are venerated by the three worlds—PHAṬ SVĀHĀ!
HŪM PHREṂ KṢOṂ KROṂ HRĪṂ VAMADAGNIMUKHI MAHĀŚAṄKHASAMĀKULE VARĀBHAYAKARE PHAṬ SVĀHĀ.

HŪṂ PHREṂ KṢOṂ KROṂ HRĪṂ! O you who are surrounded by tens of millions upon tens of millions of *pheru* spirits; O you who terrify the three heavens with the clapping of your hands; O you who possess the great dissolution-time [destruction] of the world; O you whose dancing extends your feet so that the seven continents revolve—PHAṬ SVĀHĀ!
HŪM PHREṂ KṢOṂ KROṂ HRĪṂ VAMADAGNIMUKHI MAHĀŚAṄKHASAMĀKULE VARĀBHAYAKARE PHAṬ SVĀHĀ.

HŪM PHREṂ KṢOṂ KROṂ HRĪṂ! O you who have made the serpent Śeṣa your couch by placing your feet upon him; O you who preside over the inner faculties of all living beings; O you whose essential nature is the Vedas, Āgamas, Itihāsas, Purāṇas, and the Gāvara-tantra! PHAṬ SVĀHĀ!
HŪM PHREṂ KṢOṂ KROṂ HRĪṂ! O You who dispel the anguish in the hearts of devotees;
O You who deliver all sentient beings from the three types of suffering that arise; O God of gods, the sole solar orb illuminating the lotus-heart; PHAṬ SVĀHĀ!
11a) Oṃ ai& hrī& hu& śrī& klī& strī& hu& hau& hā& kṣo& kro& phre& khphre& [subdue] all the daityas, dānavas, asuras, yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, pretas, piśācas, kuṣmāṇḍas,
ḍākinīs, śākinīs, Skanda, Vināyaka, Ghoṇaka, Kṣetrapālas, brahmarākṣasas, and gandharvas.

The paralyzing [of the effects] of secret agents, serpents, nāgas, planetary spirits, constellations, and elemental spirits; of the three kinds of portents; of thieves, fire, wild animals, and predatory beasts; of war, thunderbolts, calamities, lightning, falling meteors, and excessive rain; of poison, anti-venoms, sorcery, spells, deceit, fraud, famine, the destruction of cities, and national disturbances.
Delusion, subjugation, hatred, expulsion, possession, rivers, oceans, whirlpools, wildernesses, and whirlwinds; burning, insects, worms, moths, land-dwellers, water-dwellers, porcupines,
two-footed beings, four-footed beings, six-footed beings, eight-footed beings, many-footed beings, and the terrible darkness.
O Goddess who destroys great plagues, seizures, and harmful spirits; who takes away all possessions through illusion; who is the destroyer of the eyes of the wicked;
O Dasyu, O Deceiver, O wanderer by day, O wanderer by night, O wanderer at twilight, O horned one, O clawed one, O fanged one, O devourer, O you of manifold forms!
12a) *Drava*! O Umā, protect, protect! Guard, guard! Preserve, preserve! Sustain, sustain! Save, save!

Shelter, shelter! Lift me up, lift me up! Grant fearlessness, grant fearlessness! Be gracious, be gracious! Have compassion, have compassion! Slay my enemies, slay them! Uproot them, uproot them! Cut them down, cut them down!
Shatter! Shatter! Kill! Kill! Destroy! Strike! Strike! Expel! Expel! Paralyze! Paralyze! Grind! Grind! Annihilate! Annihilate! *Traṭ*! *Traṭ*! Dry up! Dry up! Put to flight!
Put to flight! Terrify! Delude! Delude!
12b) Bewilder, bewilder! Burst, burst! Yawn, yawn! Seize, seize! Agitate, agitate! Crush, crush! Subdue, subdue! Speed, speed! Hilī, hilī! Kicī, kicī! Burn, burn!
Devour, devour! Cut, cut! Grind to powder, grind to powder! Pound, pound! Steal, steal!

Break, break! Reduce to ashes, reduce to ashes! Attract, attract! Cast down, cast down! Make tremble, make tremble! Agitate, agitate! Cause to enter, cause to enter! Cause madness, cause madness! Terrify, terrify! Mow down, mow down! Leap upon, leap upon!
13a) Release, release! Pull out, pull out! Drink, drink! Digest, digest! Establish, establish! O *vlauṃ* in your own skull-cup!
O Blessed One, *glauṃ*, O Great Fierce One! *Āṃ*, O Tearer! *Auṃ*, O Garlanded with Heads!
Aṃ, O Mahāgrāsā! Hrīṃ, O Pārvatī! Hraṃ, O Mahābhūtinī!
Hrīṃ! O Bhujaṅgakiṇikā! Ajūṃ! O dweller in the netherworld (pātāla), you who move within the nine seed-syllables, O Kokāmukhī!
HŪṂ, O red-beaked one! HŪṂ, O Rudra-streaming one!
HŪṂ Ṛkṣakarṇī! HŪṂ Jālandharī!
HŪṂ, O you of lightning splendor! HŪṂ, O you with the moon on your forehead!

HŪṂ, you who destroy the Śabaras! HŪṂ, you who hold the *kuśa* grass in hand! HŪṂ, you who are fond of the ocean of milk! HŪṂ, you who crave the state of aesthetic absorption (*sāmarasya*)! HŪṂ, you who wander upon Mount Kailāsa!
Hūṃ! O wish-fulfilling vine of devotion! Hūṃ! O bestower of desires!
HŪṂ, to you who bestow the eightfold supernatural powers! HŪṂ, to you who grant royal sovereignty!
HŪM, O Sovereign Queen of Kings! HŪM, O She of the Lightning-like Glance!
HŪM! O you who hold a skull-bowl and are immersed in the ocean of nectar!
HŪM, O Great Ḍāmarī! HŪM, in the syllable of service through devotion!
HŪM, O bestower of the fruits of the four aims of life! HŪM OṂ, grant me enjoyment within non-duality, SVĀHĀ!
Oṃ, O you who are beyond the range [of perception], grant me accomplishment; svāhā!
Oṃ, beyond the fourth state, reveal your own nature; svāhā!
Oṃ! O you whose nature is consciousness and bliss, bestow upon me knowledge; svāhā!
Oṃ, O you whose essential nature is sound and the point, manifest the yoga; svāhā!
Oṃ, in the form consisting of pure consciousness, conceive omniscience; svāhā!
Oṃ, to the one whose body consists of mantra, who manifests the state of the essential identity of Śiva and Śakti, svāhā!
Oṃ, O small lamp of wisdom, remove the darkness of ignorance; svāhā, svāhā!
Oṃ! You who consist of the Brahman of sound, establish all knowledge within me; svāhā!
Oṃ, you who are the form of the forest fire of saṃsāra, remove birth and death, svāhā!
Oṃ, O you who are affectionate toward your devotees, pacify my miserable state; svāhā!
Oṃ, you whose nature is the triple Veda, liberate me from sin; svāhā!
Oṃ, O inner controller of all, eternal one; grant devotion unto you, svāhā!
Oṃ, O you who know all intentions, unite me with the three aims of life; svāhā!
Oṃ, O you with a gracious and beautiful countenance, grant your favor; svāhā!
Oṃ, O lioness of the forest of the Nigamas and Āgamas, dispel my sense of "mine" and ego; svāhā!
Oṃ! You who have performed the consecration by means of the nine-syllable mantra, deliver [me] from all distress, svāhā!
Oṃ, O shatterer of all calamities, bring about the welfare of us all, bring it about! Svāhā!
Oṃ śrāṃ klīṃ hsauṃ sauṃ! Homage to you, who are upon the solar seat and possessed of radiance, phaṭ!
Oṃ śrīṃ klīṃ hsauṃ sauṃ! Homage to you who are seated upon the moon and whose form is moonlight; phaṭ!
15a) Oṃ āṃ klīṃ hsauṃ sauṃ, obeisance to you who are seated upon fire and whose form is a flame, phaṭ!
Oṃ āṃ klīṃ hsauṃ sauṃ! Homage to you, the seat of Hiraṇyagarbha, the source of creation; phaṭ!
Oṃ āṃ klīṃ hsauṃ sauṃ! Homage to you who abide in the seat of Nārāyaṇa in the form of stability; phaṭ!
Oṃ āṃ klīṃ hsauṃ sauṃ! Obeisance to you, who are seated upon the great Bhairava-throne and whose form is that of universal dissolution; phaṭ!
Oṃ ā& klī& hsau& sau&! Obeisance to you who are upon the seat of the Vedas, in the form of Gāyatrī; phaṭ!
Oṃ āṃ klīṃ hsauṃ sauṃ! Obeisance to you, the sacrificial seat, whose form is the fire-oblation; phaṭ!
Oṃ āṃ klīṃ hsauṃ sauṃ! Homage to you, the embodiment of Dharma, upon the seat of conduct; phaṭ!
15b) Oṃ ā& klī& hsau& sau&! Homage to you, who are in the seat of Parjanya and have the form of rain, phaṭ!
Oṃ ā& klī& hsau& sau&! Ombilical seat, whose form is the vital breath, salutations to you, phaṭ!
Oṃ āṃ klīṃ hsauṃ sauṃ, obeisance to you, the seat of the mantra in the form of initiation, phaṭ!
Oṃ ā& klī& hsau& sau&! Homage to you, O Vratāsana, whose form is austerity! Phaṭ!
Oṃ ā& klī& hsau& sau&! Homage to you, who are upon the seat of Ananta and possess the form of the Earth; phaṭ!
Oṃ ā& klī& hsau& sau&! Obeisance to you who are the formless seat and whose nature is space; phaṭ!
Oṃ ā& klī& hsau& sau&! Homage to you, the seat of the three worlds, whose form is all powers; phaṭ!

Haṃ haṃ haṃ haiṃ haiṃ haiṃ! She who removes the fear of thieves, wild beasts in the forest, staffs, monkeys, tails, poisonous pits, fanged creatures, and hair-eating insects.
KṢAṂ KṢAṂ KṢAṂ KṢAIṂ KṢAIṂ KṢAIṂ! O slayer of deceivers, cheats, thieves, rogues, and murderers!

Hāṃ Kṣoṃ Kroṃ Hauṃ Āṃ Namaḥ to Pratyaṅgirā, who is adorned with millions upon millions of staff-like arms,
whose abode is the most terrifying cremation ground, and who is seated in the cross-legged posture upon the heart of Mahābhadra.

to her who carries away the great corpses (*mahākuṇapavāharaṇā*), to the Unconquered (*ajitā*), the Invincible (*aparājitā*), the Unobserved (*alakṣitā*), the Immeasurable (*amitā*),
the Beyond-Reach (*agocarā*), the Unobstructed (*apratihatā*), the Unarisen (*anutpannā*), and the Non-dual (*advaitā*).

O you with hundreds of millions of feet and eyes, upon whose head is a multitude of thousands; blaze, blaze! Flare up, flare up! Flash, flash! Quiver, quiver! Tremble, tremble! Crack, crack! Crackle, crackle! Roar, roar! Blow, blow! Laugh, laugh! Sing, sing! Victory, victory! Live, live! O you who wear a tiger-skin garment, you of terrifying form, you who wear a garland of severed heads!

Phreṃ Phreṃ Phreṃ Kṣoṃ Kṣoṃ Kṣoṃ Kroṃ Kroṃ Kroṃ! O Supporter of the Earth, O Upholder, O Proclaimer of Brahman, O Thou Consisting of the Nectar of Brahman, homage be to You! Homage be to You, O Pratyamgira! Homage be to You, O Siddhilakṣmī!
Homage to you, O Caṇḍakāpālinī; homage to you, the presiding deity of sovereignty!
Homage to you, O Great Illusion, who are formless yet manifold in form, whose form is the universe, who possess diverse forms, and who transcend all form.
33b) O you who destroy all asuras, daityas, and dānavas; O you who annihilate the evils of sorcery, malevolent spells, and the afflictions of planets and constellations!
O Yakṣa, Rākṣasa, Bhūta, Piśāca, Vetāla, Preta, Ḍākinī, Kūṣmāṇḍa, and Prabhañjanī!
O Gāyatrī, Sāvitrī, Mahitri, Prasavitri, Agnibhayanikṛntani, Vidya-daśanivarṣasani, and Pramardini!

She who rescues from the tempestuous winds of the ocean-going ship; she who delivers from the forest of the darkness of night; she who carries one across the perilous flood of suffering; she who pacifies the poisons of royal courts, as well as diseases such as venomous snakebites and fevers; she who removes fear from those in fear.
34a) O you who are without sin, O destroyer of sin; O you who are not dejected, O shatterer of wretchedness!
O inconceivable one who inspires thought! O unconfused one who removes delusion!

She who severs the bonds of those without kinsmen; she who uproots disease for the healthy.

To the one who bestows the marks upon that which is beyond description.
O you who manifest the unmanifest, the immortal one who bestows the fruit of immortality!
O you who bestow the words of truth upon truth; O eternal one, who brings constant bliss; O you who are unconquered by effort, who fulfills all endeavors!
34b) [She who is] unknowable by the means of valid cognition, yet bestows the establishment of the means of valid cognition.

Though devoid of qualities and form, she is to be worshipped through the worship of her qualities and limbs; she possesses the color of snow, a conch, and jasmine, has five faces and three eyes, and is formidable with her crown of tawny matted locks.
Clad in a tiger skin and wearing a garland of human skulls.

Seated upon the heart of Bhadra, bound by a yogic cloth, with two non-dual hands holding a trident, sword, severed head, goad, khaṭvāṅga, skull-cup, noose, and bell, and displaying the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness;
she possesses inconceivable and immeasurable strength and prowess, and delights in the flesh and blood of Daityas, Dānavas, and Asuras, and is victorious in battle.

She who brings about fulfillment, who bestows heaven and liberation upon her devotees, who dwells in the cremation ground, whose roar is most terrible, who utters loud and piercing laughter, the Yoginī, the Ḍākinī, Cāmuṇḍā, and Bhairavī, who moves as her companion.
35a) She whose belly hangs down greatly, the sovereign of the fourteen worlds, including the celestial realm, the earthly sphere, and the subterranean regions.
Her body consists of nine crores of mantras, and she assumes an exceedingly terrifying form.
It removes dwelling in the womb, birth, old age, and death.
The most secret of secrets, the commitment (*samaya*) of the union of the supreme and non-supreme Śiva and Śakti within the wheel of Kula and Akula,
she is hidden as the ultimate reality and bestows the fruit of liberation as the non-dual Śiva who is primordial nature.
35b) A row of thirty-two terrifying staff-bearers, by the tips of which ten million cosmic eggs were utterly pulverized.

She dwells in the center of a house consisting of four doors, four corners, three lines, an eight-spoked wheel, a twelve-petaled lotus, an eight-petaled lotus, a hexagon, and a crescent; she is to be worshipped through the King of Mantras composed of nine vowels, and she bears a form composed of the peak-syllables (kūṭa) formed from the nine vowels.
She transcends all knowledge consisting of speech.
She whose form consists of sound, the point, and the digit, who assumes the unfailing forms of the letters *va* and so forth, and who grasps and aims the thirty-three million weapons and missiles.
She is to be propitiated by the teachers of all the scriptures.
O revealer of the great khecarī mudrā!
She whose every ornament is fashioned from a great conch shell.
She who intoxicates with passion.
She who destroys all suffering and is adorned with a garland of skulls.
Her form is difficult to behold, like ten million flashes of lightning.
She devours mouthfuls of great pieces of human flesh and adorns the circle of her face with flames of fire that she vomits forth.
Surrounded by ten million times ten million jackals.
She who terrifies the three worlds with her rhythmic dancing and the clapping of her hands.
With her hands and feet extended in dance, she has the body of the serpent Śeṣa as her couch, rising and falling; she holds the corpse of Kurukulya as a parasol and wears Ulūpī as an ornament.
This bell of Aghaṇṭā is a skeleton-skeleton-rattler, with a blood-red beak and a white face,
both fierce and exceedingly fierce.
Jvālāmālinī; Bhuvanaharī.
Accompanied by Vetālas, Ananas, Skandas, and Ghaṇakas, she observes the vow of virginity.
The crusher of the lineage; the greatly fierce one; the progenitor of all seeds; the sovereign of time; the deceiver of time.
The Great Terrifying One; the Mother of the World; the Bestower of Joy to the World.

She who fondles the cocks and pigeons; she who wears a peacock feather as her ear-ornament.
Mahāḍāmarī, whose blood-red eyes roll with fury, is the sovereign goddess of the gods, who bestows supernatural power, prosperity, peace, well-being, contentment, and nourishment.
